task.description: SECURITY-REVIEWER (WF-02 Step 2c) hard gate on REQ-157.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of INV-1..INV-8 in security-invariants.md explicitly addressed (pass/fail/not-applicable with reasoning)
Capability check confirmed to run on every gated call path, no bypass found
call_service per-service parameterisation confirmed exact-match only, no prefix/wildcard grant escalation possible
The ELIXIR-DEV-flagged design deviation (data-tag dispatch instead of stored closures) independently assessed as security-neutral or flagged if not
now/fail ungated-by-design choice confirmed bounded and intentional, not a gate bypass

invariants.INV-1: NOT-APPLICABLE. Diff touches no Ecto schema, migration, or DB query -- lib/letflow/engine/lua/capabilities.ex and platform.ex are pure in-memory grant-set/dispatch logic. No tenant-scoped table or :prefix-scoped query anywhere in the diff.
invariants.INV-2: NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response type or serialization boundary touched.
invariants.INV-3: APPLIES and SATISFIED. Decision 0014 is decided and S5 has started, so this invariant is live, not deferred. Verified directly in source (not the design doc): install/2 (platform.ex:185-193) is the single fold over the closed 8-row @capability_matrix (lines 116-125); grep confirms exactly one Lua.set!(_, [:platform, ...]) call site under lib/ (platform.ex:187), and a source-level regex test (platform_test.exs:155-168) enforces this at test time, guarding against a future hand-added bypass. Every wrapper computes required_capability/2 then calls Capabilities.check!/3 (line 189) before run_stub/3 (line 190) -- check-then-stub ordering is a plain sequential two-line body inside the closure, not reorderable by any argument or code path. No ambient host access exists outside this table.
invariants.INV-4: APPLIES, SATISFIED. No secret material (API keys, tokens, DB URLs) appears anywhere in capabilities.ex or platform.ex -- confirmed by direct read plus grep for password/secret/token literals in the diff (no hits). Capability strings themselves are not secrets (they are grant identifiers, not credentials) and are handled as plain data throughout.
invariants.INV-5: NOT-APPLICABLE. No lookup-by-ID endpoint; S4 not started.
invariants.INV-6: SATISFIED by this handoff itself -- explicit statement of which invariants apply and how each is verified.
invariants.INV-7: APPLIES, SATISFIED (trivially) -- no Repo.query or any SQL in the diff; grep confirms zero hits in both files.
invariants.INV-8: APPLIES, SATISFIED. No bare {:ok, _} = match on an externally-reachable path in either file; grep confirms zero hits. now/0 (platform.ex:135-141) documents itself as unable to fail (no I/O, no user input beyond an injected time source).

specific_concerns.1_install_2_sole_bypass_check: Confirmed. `grep -rn "Lua.set!" lib/` returns only platform.ex lines 187 (the fold's call site) plus three moduledoc/comment mentions (lines 57, 114, 168) -- no other module under lib/ calls Lua.set! with a [:platform, ...] path. install/1 (line 162-164) is a thin delegate to install/2 with Capabilities.new() (empty set), not an independent registration path. There is no second entry point that installs a platform.* binding.
specific_concerns.2_check_runs_before_every_stub_all_8_row: Confirmed for all 8 rows uniformly. install/2's closure body is exactly three sequential lines: compute `required`, call `Capabilities.check!/3` (raises on denial, function never returns past this line), then call `run_stub/3`. This is the same closure body for every row in the fold -- there is no per-row branch that could skip or reorder the check, including for now/fail (whose required always resolves to :none, which check!/3 evaluates to an unconditional :ok before falling through to run_stub -- the check still executes, it just always passes).
specific_concerns.3_call_service_exact_match_no_prefix_wil: Confirmed in capabilities.ex: has?/2 (line 84-87) is literally `MapSet.member?(grant_set, capability)` -- MapSet membership is exact-value equality, with no substring/prefix logic anywhere in the module. service_capability/1 (line 145-148) builds `"service:call:" <> svc_id` via string concatenation, not a pattern/regex. Test platform_test.exs:242-270 (AC5) independently verifies a grant for 'service:call:alpha' does not authorise 'service:call:beta' -- passes.
specific_concerns.4_deviation_preserves_ordering_for_every: Assessed security-neutral. The design's raw-closure representation was infeasible (Elixir module attributes cannot escape anonymous functions -- ELIXIR-DEV quoted the real ArgumentError). The data-tag substitution (required_capability_spec/stub_spec + required_capability/2 + run_stub/3, platform.ex:102-103, 195-242) is resolved only inside install/2's fold body (line 188, 190) -- both dispatch functions are private, called from exactly one place, and cannot be invoked independent of the check!/3 call sandwiched between them. @capability_matrix itself remains a literal 8-row list (verified by capability_matrix/0 returning it and the closed-set enumeration test at platform_test.exs:135-153). No path exists where run_stub/3 is reached without required_capability/2 and check!/3 having executed first for that same call.
specific_concerns.5_now_fail_ungated_bounded: Confirmed bounded, not an accidental widening. Both rows' required is the literal atom :none (platform.ex:123-124), which Capabilities.check/3 (capabilities.ex:99) short-circuits to :ok without ever consulting the grant set -- verified in source, not just moduledoc prose. now/0's stub (run_stub(:now, ...), platform.ex:220) only calls Platform.now/0, which reads an injected TimeSource and formats it -- no state, service, or variable access. fail's stub (platform.ex:222-234) only raises a Lua.RuntimeException carrying the caller's own message string -- it reads no host state and writes nothing. Neither stub takes any code path that reaches Capabilities, ETS, Repo, or any other platform.* function. This matches decision 0014 / the R-Co matrix's stated rationale, carried into the moduledoc (platform.ex:14-28, 69-70) and enforced by platform_test.exs's moduledoc-content tests (lines 318-327) and the AC6 behavioral tests (lines 272-293).

result.notes: Read the full diff via `git show 5cdcd37 --stat` and the actual pre/post file contents directly (not the design doc or ELIXIR-DEV's self-report alone). mix/mix test were not runnable in this review environment (mix not on PATH); relied on direct code-path tracing (grep + manual read of every branch in install/2, required_capability/2, run_stub/3, check/3, check!/3, has?/2) plus ELIXIR-DEV's quoted real compile/test output (0 warnings, 39/39 new+extended lua tests passed, full suite 2131/2137 with the 6 failures independently identified as pre-existing unrelated ISS-0060 flaky tests, none touching these files). No BLOCKER found. Verdict: PASS -- no rework required.
